paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and coverage for four different language models. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)” and uses a logarithmic scale, ranging from 2<sup>0</sup> to 2<sup>8</sup>, with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis is labeled “Coverage” and uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick labels at 0.2 intervals. A dark blue line, marked with circular data points, represents the “Llama-3B” model, starting at approximately 0.42 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and increasing to roughly 0.92 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>. A green dashed line, marked with triangular data points, represents the “Llama-3B + FT” model, beginning at approximately 0.43 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and reaching around 0.93 at 2<sup>8</sup>. A light blue line, marked with diamond data points, represents “Llama-1B”, starting at about 0.22 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and rising to approximately 0.72 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>. Finally, a light green dashed line, marked with square data points, represents “Llama-1B + FT”, starting near 0.27 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and increasing to approximately 0.77 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>.
